feedback.details: All 6 files match the regex ^ADR-[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*\.md$. Sequential numbering 0001–0006 with zero gaps or duplicates. This is the strongest criterion and has been consistent since Round 2. No issues.

All 6 files contain exactly 4 H2 headings (Status, Context, Decision, Consequences) with no extras — structural compliance is perfect. All sections exceed the 50-word minimum. MD024 passes cleanly on all files. However, EVERY file fails MD022 (blanks-around-headings) with 11+ violations each. Every ## heading and most ### headings lack a blank line between the heading and the following content. For example: ADR-0001:3 (## Status), ADR-0001:6 (### Relationships), ADR-0001:9 (## Context), ADR-0001:12 (## Decision), ADR-0001:40 (## Consequences). This pattern is identical across all 6 files. The criterion explicitly states 'Validated via markdownlint MD022/MD024' and MD022 fails universally. This has been a recurring failure since Round 2 (critic-history.md:459-465, 483-494).

All 6 files pass mmdc validation with exit code 0. Three files (ADR-0002, ADR-0003, ADR-0004) contain mermaid charts that render successfully. Three files (ADR-0001, ADR-0005, ADR-0006) contain no mermaid code blocks and pass vacuously. Zero syntax warnings or errors. This has been consistently passing since Round 2.

ADR-0002 (system-context.md:60-75): Context diagram with Person node (gardener) and System node (sys), plus 4 External nodes. All edges labeled with protocol. Passes context diagram requirements. ADR-0003 (container-diagram.md:69-96): Container diagram with subgraph boundary containing 5 system containers + 1 Database node (Markdown Storage). 3 External nodes correctly placed outside subgraph. All edges labeled. Passes container diagram requirements. ADR-0004 (frontend-technology-stack.md:73-83): Has container node (Frontend System with Next.js/React, Docker technology annotation) and 3 External nodes. All edges labeled. Passes basic container requirements. No Component diagrams are present (no ADR claims to be a C3 diagram, so this is acceptable).

All 6 ADRs contain a ### Related NFRs subsection with NFR identifiers matching the regex NFR-[A-Z]+-[0-9]{2}. All 24 referenced NFR IDs across all files exist in nfr_catalog.json (NFR-USAB-01, NFR-PERF-02, NFR-RELI-01, NFR-DATA-02, NFR-DATA-03, NFR-MAINT-01). Each ADR has ≥1 valid NFR reference. No dangling or invented references. This is a significant improvement over earlier rounds where NFR citations were invalid.

The contract requires 'zero warnings' for MD001, MD022, MD023. MD001 — all 6 files pass. MD022 — ALL 6 files FAIL catastrophically with 11+ violations each. Every ## heading and most ### headings are missing blank lines before content. For example in ADR-0005: lines 3, 6, 9, 12, 25, 31, 48, 49, 57, 63 all have MD022 violations. MD023 — all 6 files pass. H1 Title Case — all 6 files have proper Title Case H1 headings. H3 sentence case — pervasive violations: 'Alternatives Considered' should be 'Alternatives considered', ADR-0005 (line 49: '### positive', line 57: '### negative') uses fully lowercase headings, which is NOT sentence case. This MD022 failure has been recurring since Round 2 and is the single largest blocker across all 6 files.

All 6 ADRs contain ### Relationships as a direct subsection of ## Status, with correct placement (H3 under H2). Five ADRs use 'None' as the value (ADR-0001 through ADR-0005). ADR-0006 (line 7) uses 'Relates to ADR-0001 (Technology Stack Selection) and ADR-0005 (Backend Technology Stack)' — both referenced files physically exist in decisions/. The exact phrase format matches the contract specification.

All 6 ADRs begin the Decision section with 'We chose to...' — matching the contract requirement. All have ### Alternatives Considered with ≥2 bullet points (ADR-0001: 3, ADR-0002: 3, ADR-0003: 3, ADR-0004: 3, ADR-0005: 4, ADR-0006: 4). All have ### Trade-offs subsections with explicit pros and cons for the selected option versus each alternative. Minor issue: ADR-0005 (line 49) uses '### positive' (lowercase) and line 57 uses '### negative' (lowercase) instead of '### Positive' and '### Negative', which is a sentence case violation.

overall_summary: Sprint 7 Round 6 shows meaningful structural improvement from previous rounds: the ADR file naming is flawless, all files have exactly the 4 required H2 headings in correct order, Relationships subsections are properly placed under ## Status, and all NFR cross-references are valid against nfr_catalog.json. Mermaid syntax passes cleanly on all 3 diagrams. However, the delivery is blocked by one pervasive and recurring issue: MD022 (blanks-around-headings) fails on every single ADR file with 11+ violations each — every ## and ### heading lacks the required blank line between the heading and the following content. This identical pattern has persisted since Round 2 and affects two separate criteria (Required ADR Sections Presence & Content and Markdown Heading Hierarchy & Formatting). Additionally, ADR-0005 uses lowercase H3 headings ('### positive', '### negative') that violate sentence case, and most files use Title Case for H3 headings ('Alternatives Considered') when sentence case ('Alternatives considered') is required. The MD022 fix is mechanical and should be trivial — adding blank lines after each heading — yet it has survived 4 rounds unaddressed.
